design: negative controls (dead circuits) and the repository's own fragile/robust golden fixtures are scored under the shipped metric (one global multiplicative factor per axis, settle-only criterion) and under a corrected one (independent per-gene LHS, agreement with the circuit's compiled Boolean fixed point)

verdict.conclusion: the sweep DOES detect instability (spread 0.7969: it fails oscillators and fragile designs), so global-vs-per-gene jitter is not the problem; but a DEAD circuit -- every gene's output drive set to zero -- scores 1.000, the maximum: the criterion asks only whether the system settles, and doing nothing settles perfectly. robustness=1.0 is therefore not evidence that a circuit works, and every circuit the pipeline actually delivers scores exactly 1.0, so the objective contributes no ranking information to NSGA-II
